title: Lost his leg to a landmine. Won India gold anyway. October 21, 2026.
excerpt: From a provisional government formed with no territory to govern, to a 93-year-old science society's first Indian woman Fellow, to a 594-kilometre expressway that doubles as an Air Force runway - October 21's five stories are about what gets built before the conditions are fully in place for it.
bodyHtml:
Every story today is about something built or achieved ahead of the conditions that would normally make it possible - a government formed before independence arrived, a training target beaten before its deadline, an institution inducting its first woman nearly a century into its history, a highway built to serve two purposes at once, and a gold medal won on a leg that wasn't there anymore.

October 21, 1943: a provisional government was announced in Singapore, with eleven ministers and no territory to govern yet

The Provisional Government of Azad Hind was announced with 11 ministers and 8 INA representatives, operating as a government-in-exile structure during the final years of British colonial rule - on its 75th anniversary in 2018, the tricolour was hoisted at Red Fort, the only time that's happened outside Independence Day.

In a 93-year-old scientific society's history, only three Indians had ever been inducted as Fellows. In 2026, the third one was a woman

Prof. Kuljeet Kaur Marhas of the Physical Research Laboratory, Ahmedabad, was elected a 2026 Fellow of The Meteoritical Society, becoming the first Indian woman to receive the honour since the society's 1933 founding, for her research on pre-solar grains and extraterrestrial material.

An India-born CEO's company just trained 5.6 million Indians in AI skills

Satya Nadella's Microsoft has trained 5.6 million people in India through its ADVANTA(I)GE India program since January 2025, enabling over 125,000 to secure jobs or start businesses - blowing past its original 10-million-by-2030 goal so decisively that Microsoft doubled the target to 20 million.

India just cut a 10-hour drive down to 6 - with a 594-kilometre expressway

The Ganga Expressway, linking Meerut to Prayagraj through 12 districts, was inaugurated April 29, 2026 at a cost of roughly Rs 36,230 crore - cutting travel time to about 6 hours and including a 3.5 km stretch built as an emergency Indian Air Force airstrip.

Lost his leg to a landmine. Won India gold anyway

Soman Rana, an Army veteran who lost a leg in a 2006 landmine blast on Line of Control duty, won gold in men's F57 shot put at the 2026 Commonwealth Games with a 13.40m throw - part of India's first-ever 1-2 finish in the event, with teammate Shubham Juyal taking silver.

Five stories, one pattern: a government built before independence existed to support it, a society's century-old membership finally including an Indian woman, a training goal beaten before its own deadline, a highway built to double as a runway, and a gold medal won on a body that had already given up a leg to the country first.
